answer: Under a compression-floor originality gate, each answer is stripped of its prompt tokens and re-encoded by a public baseline compressor; payout scales only with how far the text resists shrinking below a fixed bit budget. A farm that merely swaps in the challenge words whisper, nebula and lotus leaves its skeleton almost perfectly compressible, so every clone collapses to the same tiny code and earns nothing. Passing needs genuinely high-entropy reasoning whose bits survive re-encoding, so an attacker pays for N distinct compositions, not one shell refilled with synonyms.
